consequences: Nothing the app does can change or lock e-Sword's files; new modules appear after a rescan; the app needs macOS permission to read another app's container, which is tied to the signature.
context: The app's content is the user's e-Sword X library, including licensed Bibles (NIV, ESV) that may not be redistributed, and new modules keep being downloaded in e-Sword.
decision: Open every module where e-Sword keeps it with SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY and immutable=1; never copy module files; rescan on demand; module files are gitignored.
title: Read e-Sword modules in place, read-only and immutable

consequences: Searches take about 0.5 s; first launch spends about 30 s indexing in the background; the index is derived and safe to delete.
context: LIKE over the commentaries and dictionaries reads several hundred MB per search, about 5 s even with SQLite optimised.
decision: Build an FTS5 contentless index in the app's data folder on a background thread, per module, keyed by file size and mtime; candidates from the index, exact phrase and whole-word rules applied in Rust; LIKE fallback while a module is unindexed or for part-word searches.
title: Full-text index for commentaries and dictionaries

consequences: Entries read naturally in Obsidian; edits there survive as long as the heading and comment stay; the editor only produces Markdown it can round-trip (headings, bold, italic, lists, quotes).
context: The user keeps notes in an Obsidian vault and wants the journal in a file they own.
decision: One YYYY-MM.md per month; each entry a '## Title' heading, a hidden tes comment with id, dates, verses and tags, a generated visible meta line, then the Markdown body; one paragraph per line, never hard-wrapped.
title: Journal as monthly Markdown files

consequences: Uses the user's existing sign-in; answers stream; no tools can run; licensed Bible text is sent only when Settings allows it.
context: The user wants AI answers without managing API keys, with a model choice.
decision: Run claude -p with stream-json output, partial messages, no tools and strict MCP config, in the app's data folder, appending a Bible-study system prompt; stream text deltas to the window as events; follow-ups resume the session; chats are stored locally.
title: Ask Claude through the local Claude Code CLI

consequences: Bible chats stay tool-free. A book chat stores its folder (bookDir) so resuming uses the same cwd and session. Changing the export layout needs books::VERSION bumped so old exports are redone.
context: Reference books run to ~170k words plus charts; sending a whole book with each question floods the context, and Bible chats deliberately run claude -p with no tools.
decision: Export the book once (books.rs) as index.txt, one text file per chapter and chart PNGs under the app's data dir; run book chats with cwd set to that folder, --tools Read,Grep,Glob and --permission-mode default, so reads outside the folder need a permission print mode refuses. Send the current chapter (or ~6,000 words around the paragraph asked about) with the question.
title: Ask about a book: read-only tools confined to an exported folder

consequences: Downloaded voices are selectable; the voice setting now stores the AVSpeechSynthesisVoice identifier (names still match). A local neural voice such as Kokoro would plug in behind the same commands. Non-macOS builds have no speech.
context: WKWebView's speechSynthesis.getVoices() lists only the voices that ship with macOS; Premium and Enhanced voices downloaded in System Settings never appear, though AVSpeechSynthesisVoice.speechVoices() returns them.
decision: src-tauri/src/tts.rs speaks through AVSpeechSynthesizer on the main thread; the page sends tts_speak/tts_stop with its generation number as the utterance id and gets word ranges and end-of-utterance back as 'tts' events. Rate is scaled as WebKit did (0.5 x page rate).
title: Read aloud through AVSpeechSynthesizer, not WebKit speechSynthesis

consequences: No commentary text is pasted into prompts any more; the '+ library' chip (settings.includeCommentaries) turns the folder on. Codex shows only its final message, since earlier ones are progress notes. Study folders untouched for 60 days are pruned at start.
context: Pasting two trimmed commentary excerpts into the prompt (single verse, first question only) left the model answering 'how do the commentators differ' from memory.
decision: src-tauri/src/study.rs writes a per-chat folder (<data>/ask/studies/<chat id>): the passage in every allowed Bible, every commentary entry overlapping the passage plus chapter/book introductions, and lexicon entries for its Strong's numbers; dictionaries are exported whole once (<data>/ask/dictionaries, redone when a module file changes) in the background at start and after a rescan. The chat runs in that folder with read-only search (Claude: Read/Grep/Glob plus --add-dir for dictionaries; Codex: read-only sandbox) and is told to answer from it and name sources.
title: Ask answers from the library by searching exported files

consequences: Codex answers arrive whole, not streamed. Codex's read-only sandbox can read outside a chat's folder; it is only told to stay inside. Claude chats keep their data/claude working folder so old sessions still resume; Codex uses data/codex.
context: Ask only ran the Claude Code CLI. Codex CLI can run non-interactively too (codex exec --json, resume by thread id), and the app should not show Ask when it cannot answer.
decision: src-tauri/src/assistant/ holds the shared prompt and process tracking, with claude.rs and codex.rs per CLI; a model id starting with 'claude' goes to Claude Code, anything else to Codex. Codex runs with --ignore-user-config --ignore-rules in the read-only sandbox, instructions passed as -c developer_instructions, and its models are read from the model cache Codex keeps in its home folder (entries with visibility=list). src/assistant.ts checks what is installed; with neither CLI every Ask control is hidden.
title: Ask supports Claude Code and Codex; hidden when neither is installed

consequences: Retake with make screenshots after any visual change. The Ask shot is a stored answer (tools/screenshots/ask-chat.json), regenerate it by hand if the answer format changes. Needs Screen Recording permission for the terminal.
context: Screenshots were taken by hand, one per screen, and went stale with every look change; macOS embedded the display's colour profile, which tinted them in browsers.
decision: tools/screenshots.py launches the dev build (cargo build --no-default-features, page from the Vite server) once per scene and theme with TES_SCENE set; src/scene.ts applies it (settings, screen, passage, a fixture chat, a still player) and api.ts stops all saving. The window is fixed at 1440x900, captured with screencapture -l by PID, resized to 1400 wide and saved without an ICC profile. Docs use <picture> with light and dark sources.
title: Screenshots are taken by a script, from scenes, in both themes

consequences: New ways of moving around should call these functions, not set screen or state directly, or back will skip them. DocReader filling in a book's chapter replaces the entry instead of pushing one.
context: Back and forward only recorded Bible passages, so they did nothing in Word Study, Search or between screens.
decision: state.tsx keeps a stack of places (screen, passage, open book chapter, Word Study target, search). Every navigation goes through navigate(): go, open, openDoc, closeDoc, studyWord, searchText, startEntry, setPending. Word Study's target may be an English word, so a lookup list is a place; Search runs a new query through searchText. back/forward restore a place without pushing.
title: One back/forward history of places for the whole app

consequences: New buttons and controls get a title as a matter of course. Disabled buttons show no tooltip (WebKit sends no pointer events to them). Tooltips are off in screenshot mode.
context: macOS's native tooltips look out of place beside the app's popovers; the app now has its own (Tooltips in src/ui.tsx), and a mix of the two looks broken.
decision: Every tooltip is the custom one. Give an element a title (or, for an icon-only button, an aria-label) and Tooltips shows it in the popover style, everywhere in the app. Do not build other tooltip components, and do not rely on native tooltips; keep title text short and useful (what it does, and its shortcut).
title: Always use the app's custom tooltip

consequences: About 8x faster (0.33 s). Totals can be a few percent higher than a strict text check, since the index also matches a phrase across punctuation; the library test allows that.
context: Searching a common word ("light", about 20,800 matches) took ~2.8 s in a release build, far longer in dev: every indexed match was loaded and converted to plain text just to be counted.
decision: For an indexed whole-word search, candidate_rows counts the index's matches in SQL (with the book-range filter) and loads only the rows shown (limit + 10), which are still text-checked for their snippets.
title: Search counts come from the index, not a text check of every match

consequences: A book renamed in its module breaks its labels' links. Notes on a chapter are found by matching the book's title and chapter title.
context: Paragraphs of reference books and devotionals needed the verse tools (highlight, bookmark, note, listen, ask, copy) and a study pane, but journal entries link verses by readable strings and highlights are keyed by book.chapter.verse.
decision: src/docref.ts: a journal entry links a paragraph by the label 'Book title › Chapter ¶n' (or ¶n–m, or no ¶ for the chapter) in its verses list, so the Markdown stays readable; highlights use the key doc|module|title|para in the same store; bookmarks carry a DocSpot. DocReader selects paragraphs on click (not on a word), shows the verse toolbar as icons, and has a study pane with Notes, Dictionary and Ask (settings.docTab).
title: Book paragraphs are linked, highlighted and bookmarked like verses

consequences: No reminder once the app is quit. Clicking the notification does not start Quiet time; the menu's Start Quiet Time item does.
context: The window hides rather than closes and a hidden WKWebView throttles timers, so a JS timer can't be trusted to fire at the reminder time.
decision: src/tray.tsx sends a TrayState (today's reading, done, place, reminder on and time) via set_tray once saved settings and plans have loaded; src-tauri/src/tray.rs rebuilds the menu-bar menu from it and a thread checks every 30s, firing a notification within 2h after the time, at most once a day (last fired date kept in the store as reminder.json). Menu choices come back to the page as 'tray' events.
title: Quiet time reminder is timed in Rust, not the page

consequences: Needs the apple-events entitlement and NSAppleEventsUsageDescription (src-tauri/Entitlements.plist, Info.plist); the first use prompts for Automation permission. Catalogue songs not in the library can't be chosen. Choosing takes 15-35s with ~1500 candidates, so it starts when the session starts and a day's choice is cached in memory.
context: Worship songs for Quiet time should suit the day's reading. Apple Music catalogue playback needs MusicKit and a paid developer token; the Music app's library can be driven by osascript with no account setup.
decision: List the library's Christian/gospel/worship-genre songs via JXA, have the assistant choose by number from that numbered list (so it can only name songs that exist), queue them in the app's own playlist 'Two-edged Sword · Quiet time' (deleted and remade each time, never touching other playlists) and play it. Pause/skip only act while that playlist is playing. Random choice when no assistant or the answer can't be parsed.
title: Quiet time worship songs come from the Music library, picked by number

consequences: Chats from before this change whose index points at the shared dictionaries folder can no longer read dictionaries. The user's own Claude Code settings still load and could widen what it reads; documented, not closed.
context: The Licensed translations switch only swapped the Bible used for the passage; licensed commentaries, lexicons and dictionaries still went into the chat folder, Compare and Search sent licensed verses, and book chats sent licensed books. Dictionaries were shared via --add-dir, so any of them could be read.
decision: Renamed to Licensed text. When off, isLicensed modules of every kind are withheld: Bibles fall back to public-domain text or send the reference only; study export takes an exclude list; dictionaries are hard-linked per chat so only allowed ones are reachable and --add-dir is gone; Compare, Search and book chats send no licensed text.
title: Licensed text off withholds every licensed module from Ask, not just Bibles

consequences: A refused action ends agy's turn with no answer; the app reports that as an error. The user's own Antigravity rules files still load, and agy keeps its own history in its own history folder in the home directory. If agy stops enforcing agent tool lists, web search returns silently.
context: Gemini CLI was retired for personal accounts in June 2026 in favour of Antigravity CLI (agy). agy has no flag to limit tools, uses web search unprompted (search_web is not a permission action, so settings can't deny it), and its project settings file wasn't honoured in print mode.
decision: Each run writes .agents/agents/tes-ask.md into its working folder: a mainAgent with inheritMcp false and tools limited to view_file, grep_search, find_by_name, list_dir (or [] outside a folder chat), and runs agy -p --agent tes-ask --sandbox. Tested: the tools list is enforced (the model reports no web search tool); reads outside the folder, commands and read_url are refused in print mode. Model ids are prefixed agy: since it also offers Claude models.
title: Antigravity CLI for Ask, confined by a per-run custom agent

consequences: An organisation's Copilot policy can block the CLI (seen on this account at first). Instructions in the user turn are weaker than a system prompt. No model choice beyond Auto.
context: copilot -p has --available-tools, --disable-builtin-mcps and --no-custom-instructions, but no system-prompt flag and no way to list models (not in -p, errors or ACP session/new).
decision: Folder chats get --available-tools=view,grep,glob; others get view only in an empty working folder, because an empty --available-tools= means every tool (it tried web_fetch in testing). Ask's instructions open the first message; follow-ups resume with --resume. One model, copilot:auto.
title: GitHub Copilot CLI for Ask: --available-tools, instructions in the first message, Auto only

consequences: An external edit that keeps both size and mtime (rare) would be missed until the next change. Sync tools that go by mtime rather than file events could skip an upload; OneDrive's File Provider sees the rename.
context: The user wants editing an entry not to change its month file's mtime (they also asked this of bulk retagging); an old month shouldn't look new to Finder, Obsidian's sort or backups.
decision: write_month reads the file's mtime before the atomic write and sets it back afterwards; a new month file keeps its creation time. Change detection is unaffected: stamp() also compares sizes, the app reloads after its own saves, and other editors change the mtime themselves.
title: Journal saves keep the month file's modified time

consequences: A misspelling that happens to be a KJV word isn't caught. Without a KJV module nothing changes. The set isn't rebuilt on Rescan.
context: The journal's macOS spell checker flagged KJV spellings (maketh, remaineth, names) and the grammar checker flagged KJV English (he maketh me, thou art); the user had been adding KJV words to the shared macOS dictionary one by one.
decision: At start a background thread reads every word of the library's KJV (a Bible with abbreviation KJV, tags stripped) into a set (about 12.8k words); spell::check drops flagged words in it. A sentence with grammar issues is skipped when it has a marker (thee, thou, hath, unto…) or a KJV word macOS flags. A check that comes before the read has finished does the read itself, since the editor caches results per paragraph. The user's learned KJV words were unlearned (16).
title: The KJV's words count as spelled right in the journal

consequences: The journal stays the user's own. A new translation is one candidates run, one review and one build. The file is not in the repo, so it is rebuilt from the work folder if lost.
context: Wayne wanted every place the NIV departs in meaning from the KJV flagged, and the same for other translations later. There are hundreds per translation.
decision: tools/variances/ finds candidates by script, agents review them against review.md, and build.py writes variances-<module>.json to the app data folder. The reading pane shows a marker in Verse layout from that file. Records hold only the reference, category, a short change and a note: never the translation's text, which is read from the module.
title: Translation variances live in a per-module data file, not the journal

consequences: About 5% of words, where SEDRA's text differs from the 1905 Bible Society text, are left without a gloss; glosses are dictionary senses, with a COMMON table overriding SEDRA for the commonest little words; the tokenizer counts Syriac as an original language
context: The Peshitta has no Strong's numbers (Syriac has none); ETCBC's syrnt (MIT, from SEDRA 3) tags every NT word, and SEDRA IV's API has English glosses, but SEDRA calls itself non-commercial and its site says all rights reserved
decision: tools/syriac/build.py lines syrnt's words up with peshitta.bbli per chapter, takes glosses from SEDRA's API (cached), and writes peshitta+.bbli in INT+'s <div> markup; the module is built on the user's machine only
title: Peshitta+ is built locally from syrnt and SEDRA, never committed

consequences: About 2% of words have no English; glosses are dictionary senses and some tags are wrong; the builder needs a ~1 GB venv; tokenize's <div> path now takes the box's word in any script
context: No Vulgate with per-word English exists; Open Words (Python Whitaker) failed common words (creavit) and picked absurd senses (caelum: beer)
decision: tools/latin tags each verse with Stanza's PROIEL Latin model (in-context lemma and grammar) in a cached venv, and takes the most frequent Whitaker DICTLINE entry's first sense for the lemma, with a MEANINGS table for Biblical senses and case-aware personal pronouns; -que is split off as and
title: Latin+ Bibles are tagged by Stanza and glossed from Whitaker

consequences: About 39% of Onkelos/Jonathan words and 34% of Ps-Jon's are paired; 9-12% have no English; Jastrow glosses are often off; the tooltip says Hebrew or Jastrow so a reader can tell
context: No lemmatised Targum with English is freely available (CAL isn't downloadable); Jastrow is, but its first gloss is often a homograph's
decision: tools/targum pairs each Targum word with a cognate word of the same verse in WLC+ (consonants, prefixes and endings set aside, Aramaic-Hebrew letter correspondences, an order-keeping best pairing, EQUIV for non-cognates like יי for יהוה/אלהים) and takes its English and Strong's number; unpaired words take COMMON (the ~250 commonest) or Jastrow's first gloss after stripping affixes, preferring Aramaic (ch.) entries
title: Targum+ glosses come from pairing with WLC+, then a table, then Jastrow

consequences: 7850 of 7957 verses, 83% word overlap with Challoner; ~107 verses lost at page gaps are left out; scattered OCR errors remain; the KJV History Rheims card now matches it as the text itself
context: No clean digital 1582 Rheims NT exists; Bible Support's '1582' module is Challoner's text; its file 11077 has only Google Books' OCR of Bagster's 1872 parallel edition, with verse numbers mangled and column edges lost
decision: tools/rheims aligns the OCR word stream with drc.bbli (Challoner keeps most 1582 wording) to find verse boundaries, searches near neighbours for verses read out of order, fills from the RTF where its reading matches better, and corrects only non-dictionary misreadings to Challoner's word in the same slot
title: Rheims 1582 is rebuilt from Google Books OCR, verses found by aligning with Challoner

consequences: Ginsburg lacks 5 verses where its sources stop short; the Beza transcription has a few non-Beza readings (Luke 2:22); LXX Exodus 35-40 follows the Greek order and 230 KJV verses have no Greek; the Apocrypha (67+) are in the LXX file but the app shows books 1-66 only
context: The Rabbinic Bible, Beza and Sixtine Septuagint cards had only stand-ins; research found Ginsburg 1894 (follows Ben Chayyim, Apache-2.0), a Beza 1598 transcription on textus-receptus.com, and eBible's Greek Brenton (Vatican/Sixtine text)
decision: tools/ginsburg numbers Ginsburg's words by aligning them with the WLC then morphhb's VerseMap; tools/beza fetches the wiki (cached), strips notes, re-divides 35 chapters by alignment with TR+ and fills two mislabelled pages from the wiki's Scrivener; tools/lxx maps LXX to KJV through SIL's versification tables plus hand rules (Proverbs, 3 Kgdms 20/21, Malachi), joining lettered additions to the verse before
title: Three more KJV sources built: Ginsburg (for Bomberg), Beza 1598, Greek Brenton (for the Sixtine)

consequences: If printing is ever added it needs another shortcut (⌘⇧P). The app shows in Control Centre's Now Playing while reading. A journal entry being read is read-only until the player stops.
context: Space plays in the readers but types a space in the journal's editor, so the player needed a key that works everywhere. The F keys are media keys on a Mac keyboard and only reach the webview with fn held.
decision: ⌘P / F8 play or pause anywhere (starting the screen's text via useListenKey when nothing is playing); F7 / F9 go to the previous / next chapter, book chapter or journal entry. src-tauri/src/media.rs registers MPRemoteCommandCenter handlers and sets Now Playing while reading, so the hardware keys come to the app. ⌘P shadows Print, which the app doesn't have. During a Quiet time Worship part the F keys and media events are ignored so they stay the music player's.
title: Player keys: ⌘P and F8 play/pause, F7/F9 previous/next, via macOS media keys too

consequences: Search's Whole Bible range is now 1-78; an Apocrypha range was added. Nothing marks the Greek additions inside Daniel 3 (the Song of the Three) or Esther's inline additions in the Latin Vulgate, since they are verses, not chapters.
context: Nine Bibles in the library (Douay-Rheims, the Vulgates, Bishops', Brenton, the Septuagints) carry the Apocrypha as books 67-78, and several add chapters to canonical books (Esther 11-16, Daniel 13-14, Psalm 151), but the app knew only the 66 books, so none of it could be reached.
decision: bible.ts keeps BOOKS as the 66 (plans, Word Study rely on it) and adds APOCRYPHA with e-Sword's numbers; isApocrypha(b, c) also covers the extra chapters. stepChapter takes each Bible's own chapter counts (bibleSizes) and follows a reading order with the Apocrypha between Malachi and Matthew, as the 1611 KJV and Bishops' printed them. A yellow ApoPill marks them in the reader, picker, Compare, search and player. e-Sword's 'Man' abbreviation isn't a parse alias, so 'man 3' in prose doesn't link. Plans stay canonical (chaptersOf drops apocryphal chapters).
title: The Apocrypha: e-Sword's books 67–78, read between the Testaments, marked yellow

consequences: Renaming a theme changes its tag for new entries; old entries keep the old tag. Chats started before names were set don't get theme tags. A model that ignores the instruction just yields no tags.
context: Highlight colours can be named (Settings › Highlights) as themes; journal entries and Ask answers needed to be tagged with the same themes consistently.
decision: A theme's journal tag is its name slugified (themeTag in state.tsx), not a separate setting. Ask's first message carries the theme list and asks the model to end every answer with a 'Themes: #tag' line; splitThemes in Ask.tsx hides that line and uses its known tags when an answer goes into the journal.
title: Highlight themes: tags from names, and Ask names them in a hidden last line

consequences: docs/*.md stays the one source; the release build needs pandoc. Screenshots in the help are the docs' own, so the public-domain-only rule for committed images covers them.
context: Apple's guidance for Mac help is a Help Book registered in Info.plist, which Help Viewer shows and the Help menu's search field searches. The user guides already exist as docs/*.md.
decision: tools/helpbook.py converts the user guides (not development.md) with pandoc into src-tauri/gen/help/Two-edged Sword.help, with hiutil search indexes; beforeBuildCommand runs it and bundle.macOS.files copies it into Contents/Resources. The generated book is gitignored. Help > Two-edged Sword Help (⌘?, set on the AppKit item since accelerators can't spell it) calls showHelp:; a dev build, which has no bundle, opens the built index.html in the browser.
title: Help menu opens an Apple Help Book built from docs/

consequences: The guide an agent reads always matches the running build. A chat without a folder can now read files in its per-CLI working folder, which holds only help/ (and Antigravity's agent file). A new user guide in docs/ must be added to GUIDES in help.rs and PAGES in tools/helpbook.py.
context: Ask agents couldn't answer questions about the app itself, and loading the guides into every prompt would cost context on every question.
decision: src-tauri/src/help.rs builds docs' user guides into the app (include_str) and writes them, screenshots stripped, to help/ in each chat's working folder with an index.txt of files and sections; the system prompt tells the agent to search help/ for questions about the app. Chats that had no folder (Compare, Word Study, search) now run with the same read-only tools in their per-CLI working folder, so the no-tools branches in the four CLIs are gone.
title: Ask searches the user guide, so every chat gets read-only search

consequences: Tools read inputs through tools/modules.py find(); scripts still reading e-Sword modules (beza/plus, lxx/plus) are personal-use until moved to STEPBible. Module ids stay the same so settings and preferences keep working.
context: e-Sword's licence (§3–5) forbids distributing its modules, even public-domain ones, as part of any package, or hosting them; the app depended on e-Sword X being installed.
decision: The library reads three folders in order, first wins: the app's own Modules folder under Application Support (tools/ writes there), e-Sword X's library (on by default, a Library switch turns it off, skipped quietly if absent), and modules bundled in the app. A public-domain core will be built from open sources (CrossWire, STEPBible, Open Scriptures) and bundled; nothing from e-Sword is shipped.
title: An app-owned modules folder, with e-Sword X's library optional

consequences: About 45 MB in the bundle. The files are not committed; make dev and the release build run it with --if-missing. e-Sword's copies still win while Read e-Sword X is on, so the bundled ones show only without it.
context: The app should work without e-Sword X, and e-Sword's modules can't be shipped. CrossWire was unreachable when this was built.
decision: tools/core/build.py builds kjv, kjv+ (eBible.org eng-kjv2006, CrossWire's KJV in USFM), strong (Open Scriptures' Strong's Greek XML 1.4 and Hebrew XML, public domain; the Hebrew outline and TWOT numbers are left out), kjc (counted from kjv+) and tsk (CrossWire TSK 1.5 via the man4christ IMP mirror) into src-tauri/modules, bundled as Resources/modules. Spellings follow e-Sword's (ae for æ, straight apostrophes) so searches match.
title: The built-in core modules: KJV, KJV+, Strong's, KJC and TSK from public-domain sources

consequences: lxx/plus still needs e-Sword's Greek OT+: every tagged Septuagint comes from CATSS, whose licence is restrictive. Rebuilt Beza+ and LXX+ differ from the TR+/INT+ builds in about 7% of numbers, mostly pronouns and εἰμί now in Strong's form numbers.
context: beza/plus and lxx/plus read e-Sword's TR+, INT+, BYZ+ and WH+ for Strong's numbers and grammar. TAGNT (CC BY 4.0) has every edition's words with numbers and Robinson codes, but numbers verses as the NRSV, and gives forms of ἐγώ, σύ and εἰμί their headword's number.
decision: tools/stepbible.py reads TAGNT, keyed by the KJV's verse (its [c.v] where given), and takes the last Alt Strongs number for G1473, G3165, G4771 and G1510 (μου G3450, ἐστιν G2076). beza/plus uses it alone (TR, then Byz, then any edition); lxx/plus uses it for the NT side. beza/build keeps TR+ when present, since correcting the wiki needs Stephanus' readings, and otherwise divides verses by TAGNT's TR without correcting.
title: Greek NT tagging from STEPBible's TAGNT, with classic Strong's form numbers

consequences: Anyone passing on the app, changed or not, must do so under the GPL with its source. The Bible texts and books are not covered: each keeps its own terms, and nothing of e-Sword's is distributed.
context: The owner wanted the app to stay free, in e-Sword's spirit (e-Sword itself is proprietary freeware, not GPL). Every dependency's licence (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, MPL-2.0, Zlib, ISC, Unicode, OFL fonts) is compatible.
decision: LICENSE is the GNU GPL v3 text; package.json and Cargo.toml say GPL-3.0-or-later; the bundle's copyright line (the About box) names it; Settings shows it under the version; features.md › Licence and credits (a Help page) lists the modules' own terms and the dependencies'.
title: The app is GPL-3.0-or-later

consequences: Bethel and Beth-el find each other in every Bible, commentary and dictionary. A search for one half ('Beth') no longer finds the hyphenated name. Dashes between words (' - ') still count.
context: The built-in KJV prints the 1769 hyphenated names (Beth-el, Beer-sheba); e-Sword's KJV writes Bethel, so a search for Bethel missed them. The texts should stay as printed.
decision: search.rs unhyphen() drops a hyphen with a letter or digit on both sides, from the query and from the text before matching (offsets mapped back for the snippet); the LIKE filter compares replace(col, '-', ''); the full-text index stores the unhyphened text (its stamp gains a version, 2-, so every module is indexed again once).
title: Search ignores hyphens inside words, rather than changing the texts

consequences: The DMG grows by about 15 MB. Verse coverage matches e-Sword's Henry except Prov 11:20, which CrossWire lacks. A newer CrossWire release could shift slots: rerun the QA (refs valid, paragraphs balanced, no stray markup, coverage) before shipping one.
context: A new user had no commentary or dictionary besides the TSK and Strong's. e-Sword's copies can't be passed on. CrossWire's MHC and Easton are public domain (from CCEL), but their links are wrong in places: Easton links follow-on references to the wrong book, and MHC resolves some 'v.'/'ver.' against the book cited before.
decision: tools/core builds henry.cmti and easton.dcti from CrossWire's rawzip modules, with the same ids as e-Sword's so e-Sword's copies take their place. References are re-read from their visible text (Easton) or repaired against the passage in hand (MHC), and every link is checked against the KJV's verses; anything still impossible is left as text. The Bible text each MHC section opens with is dropped, as e-Sword does. Easton misspellings found by diffing against e-Sword's copy are corrected by a checked list.
title: Ship Matthew Henry and Easton's built in, from CrossWire

consequences: Anyone with a matching module sees the marks. A rebuilt list shows at once from the data folder; copying it into src-tauri/variances/ ships it with the next release. Records quote a few words of each translation, within the publishers' quotation allowances.
context: The ≠ lists lived only in the app's data folder, so no one else saw them; eight translations are now reviewed across the whole Bible.
decision: src-tauri/variances/ holds each variances-<module>.json and the app bundles it as Resources/variances; store::variances reads the data folder's copy first, then the bundled one, for the reading pane and Ask.
title: The app ships the difference lists

consequences: make lint must pass with zero warnings; make fmt formats everything. Every source file carries the copyright notice and an SPDX GPL-3.0-or-later line.
context: The code had no formatter or linter config; long lines were the house style.
decision: rustfmt and Prettier at 140 columns; clippy defaults with -D warnings; ESLint recommended + typescript-eslint + only the classic react-hooks rules (rules-of-hooks, exhaustive-deps), since the React Compiler rules assume a compiler the app does not use. Deliberately keyed effect deps keep an eslint-disable comment.
title: Lint and format with rustfmt, clippy, Prettier and ESLint

consequences: Song name, artist, album and length are sent to lrclib.net, and name/artist to itunes.apple.com when Music has no artwork. Framed pages can't be reached into, so inversion also inverts their pictures. Screenshot scenes use a public-domain hymn and the app icon (songFile) rather than live Music.
context: Online devotionals opened in a separate window, hiding the Quiet time bar; Music's own lyrics view can't be embedded and Apple Music's synced lyrics can't be read by another app.
decision: Online devotionals are framed (iframe) in the reading column, inverted by CSS filter in the dark theme per site (Settings.webInvert); sites added by the user are checked for X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors with curl and open in their own window if they refuse framing. Lyrics come from LRCLIB (timed), else the song's saved lyrics; artwork from Music via AppleScript raw data, else the iTunes search API; flames at the song's BPM (default 72) when there are none, since the app can't hear Music's audio.
title: Quiet time shows third-party pages and lyrics inside the reading column

consequences: One extra call per answer on the chat's model; the hint appears a few seconds after the answer. No Rust command needed.
context: Wanted Brainstead's next-turn hint in Ask. This app has no per-job models and already has askOnce for one-off questions (worship, closing verse).
decision: After each answer without an error, askOnce sends the chat's last three exchanges (Themes line stripped) to the chat's own model and takes the first line of the reply. Shown as the empty box's placeholder; → or Tab types it. Kept in AskPanel state only, never saved, and dropped once the chat's message count changes. Switch: settings.askSuggest, default on.
title: Ask suggests the next question with a second call

consequences: Needs macos-private-api for the transparent window. The window must read its state after its listeners are registered, or a state sent at start-up is missed. Screenshot scenes take tray: true.
context: Wanted a richer menu-bar menu like Brainstead's and Keepr's. Here plans, streaks and settings live in the main window's state, not in Rust.
decision: The icon opens a small webview window (label tray, index.html?view=tray, src/TrayWindow.tsx) under it, closed when it loses focus. The main window still computes TrayState (src/tray.tsx) and sends it to Rust; Rust keeps it, emits tray-state to the window, and serves it with tray_info. Choices go through tray_do: open, quit and login in Rust, the rest as tray events to the main window.
title: Menu-bar window instead of a native menu

consequences: All 44 docs images in about 80s with nothing on screen. The window buttons are drawn, not captured: if macOS changes them, chrome() needs new measurements. Screenshots are macOS only.
context: Retaking the screenshots showed each app window on screen in turn, one at a time, and needed Screen Recording permission and a compiled window_id helper. Brainstead had already solved this.
decision: Ported from Brainstead: in screenshot mode (TES_SCENE) the main or tray window has alpha 0, ignores the mouse, the app leaves the Dock and never takes focus. The app saves WKWebView's takeSnapshot as a TIFF to TES_SNAPSHOT after TES_SNAPSHOT_AFTER seconds; tools/screenshots.py draws the unfocused window buttons and rounded corners back on (measured from the old captures), retries a blank shot from a fresh launch, and runs 4 apps at once (-j). window_id.swift is gone.
title: Screenshots are taken unseen, from the webview's snapshot

consequences: One copy of the text still: docs/ is the guide on GitHub, the drawer and Ask's help/ folder. macOS's Help-menu search no longer finds the guides; the drawer's own search does. A new screen needs a SCREEN_HELP entry in src/guides.ts.
context: The Help menu opened an Apple Help Book built with pandoc and hiutil; helpd cached old books by version, so installs had to clear its cache, and help meant leaving the app. Brainstead's ? drawer shows help beside the screen.
decision: Help is a drawer in the window (src/Help.tsx) showing the docs/ guides, imported at build time and split by ## section, opened on the current screen's section by ?, the top bar's ? button or ⌘?. The Help Book, helpbook.py and pandoc are gone; make help now runs tools/helpcheck.py.
title: In-app help drawer replaces the Apple Help Book

consequences: Changing or removing it must go through withFinale, which takes the old one off the last day. Psalm-and-Proverb plans have no end, so get no last reading.
context: A favourite passage to read at the very end of a sequence plan (e.g. Proverbs 3:5-6).
decision: SequencePlan.finale records it, and withFinale also appends it to days[last], so the calendar, Quiet time and ticking off need no changes; partKeys gives a passage in a chapter the day already has its own key (20.3:5).
title: A plan's last reading is kept in its last day

consequences: It counts towards the day being read in Quiet time, like any other Bible part. Opening a single part from the today card doesn't include it.
context: A plan can have a favourite passage (e.g. Proverbs 3:5-6) read every day, at the end.
decision: Plan.finale holds it; quietSteps adds it as a bible step keyed 'finale', after worship and before the closing verse. The plan's days and the today card are untouched.
title: A favourite passage is a Quiet time step, not part of the plan's days

consequences: Chapter songs never use up Quiet time's choices. Quiet time playing clears the chapter's list, so the Lyrics page shows the right reasons.
context: A reader button picks worship songs for the open Bible or book chapter, reusing worship.ts and music.rs.
decision: pickChapterSongs builds on the same choose() as Quiet time, without the 14-day rest and without markPlayed. The one app playlist is renamed 'Two-edged Sword' (the old 'Two-edged Sword · Quiet time' one is deleted on play), so Music's 'ours' check covers both.
title: Songs for a chapter share Quiet time's picker and playlist, and don't count as played

consequences: Pages must be set to main, /docs. make site after make screenshots, or the page's pictures go stale. helpcheck only globs *.md, so the extra files in docs/ don't affect make help.
context: A marketing page was wanted, hosted on GitHub Pages, with animated screenshots and no framework. GitHub Pages serves a branch's root or its docs/ folder; the root index.html is the Vite app's.
decision: docs/index.html with docs/site/{landing.css,landing.js,img/}; docs/.nojekyll so the Markdown guides are served raw. The pictures are WebP copies of the dark screenshots made by make site (cwebp), so the page loads about 3 MB rather than 20. Animation is CSS plus a small script: screenshots zoom to a spot or swap per step, while the section is on screen.
title: The product page lives in docs/ as plain HTML for GitHub Pages
